content.comment_body: [product_name] [version_no], [article_no]. When I convert my file from one format to another and save, I receive a warning: "The diagram exceeds BM location memory limit. Only block location is saved." What does this mean? I can still transfer the program to the controller without issues. My hard drive has plenty of space (97k remaining), and I encounter the same warning when saving to an empty 8GB microSD card.

The message is just a warning, not an error. The diagram's block arrangement relies on specific layout memory with a size limit (approximately 30,000 units). If the diagram contains many blocks and separate elements, this memory may be insufficient. However, this does not affect program execution or transfer to the controller—the program works fine. The downside is when you read the program back from the controller to the PC, the blocks may be arranged randomly and previous connections may be closed. So this is purely a graphical issue. It’s important to keep the original version of your program safe.
Alright, thanks! I know that reading programs from [product_name] has always mixed up block arrangement, at least since [article_no]. Good to hear it’s just a warning.

analysis.insight_summary: The primary concern raised is a warning about exceeding BM location memory limit when converting and saving diagrams in [product_name] software. Users are unsure if this refers to hardware storage, but it is actually related to graphical layout memory for diagram arrangements. The warning does not affect sending the program to the device or its operation, but only changes how the diagram looks when retrieved from the hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to save diagrams without memory-related warnings, expecting available storage space to be sufficient. They also seek clearer distinction between warnings and errors in system messages.
